name: Label and select pods
objective: CKAD core: label and annotate objects, and target them with equality + set-based selectors. Add/overwrite/remove labels, bulk-label via a selector, set-based matching, matchExpressions selectors, annotations, and a selector-mismatch diagnose-fix. Graded exactly.

questions.title: Add a label
questions.teach:
`kubectl label <kind>/<name> key=value` attaches a label (key/value metadata used for selecting and grouping objects).

**Gotcha:** labelling an existing key without `--overwrite` fails — add fails loudly rather than clobbering.
questions.prompt:
In `labels-learn`, add the label `env=prod` to pod `frontend`.

Target: pod `frontend` has label `env=prod`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn label pod frontend env=prod
kubectl -n labels-learn get pod frontend --show-labels

questions.title: Overwrite and remove a label
questions.teach:
Change an existing label with `kubectl label --overwrite key=newvalue`; remove one with `kubectl label <obj> key-` (trailing dash).

**Gotcha:** without `--overwrite`, relabelling an existing key errors; `key-` (not `key=`) is how you delete a label.
questions.prompt:
Pod `legacy` in `labels-learn` has labels `env=dev` and `deprecated=true`. **Overwrite** `env` to `prod`, and **remove** the `deprecated` label.

Target: pod `legacy` has `env=prod` and no `deprecated` label.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n labels-learn label --overwrite pod legacy env=prod` and `kubectl -n labels-learn label pod legacy deprecated-`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn label --overwrite pod legacy env=prod
kubectl -n labels-learn label pod legacy deprecated-
kubectl -n labels-learn get pod legacy --show-labels

questions.title: Bulk-label via a selector
questions.teach:
Label many objects at once by targeting them with `-l <selector>`: `kubectl label pods -l app=shop tier=web` labels every pod matching `app=shop`.

**Gotcha:** `-l` on `kubectl label` selects *which* objects to label — it doesn't set that label.
questions.prompt:
In `labels-learn`, add the label `tier=web` to **all** pods that match `app=shop` (there are two), in one command.

Target: every `app=shop` pod has `tier=web`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn label pods -l app=shop tier=web
kubectl -n labels-learn get pods -l app=shop --show-labels

verification.description: all app=shop pods now have tier=web

questions.title: Set-based selector targeting
questions.teach:
Set-based selectors match against a set of values: `-l 'release in (beta,rc)'`, `notin (...)`, or `key`/`!key` (exists / not-exists). Use them to target a subset.

**Gotcha:** quote the selector in the shell; equality (`=`,`!=`) and set-based (`in`,`notin`) can be combined with commas.
questions.prompt:
In `labels-learn`, add `canary=yes` to every pod whose `release` is **in (beta, rc)** — using a set-based selector. The `release=stable` pod must NOT get it.

Target: `rel-beta` and `rel-rc` have `canary=yes`; `rel-stable` does not.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn label pods -l 'release in (beta,rc)' canary=yes
kubectl -n labels-learn get pods -L release -L canary
